Metadata.title: Online 2D CAD with AutoCAD commands — MellowCAD
Metadata.description: 2D drafting in your browser with the commands, aliases and object snaps AutoCAD users know. No install, no sign-up; drawings stay on your device.
Metadata.drawDescription: Precision 2D drafting with the commands, snaps and keyboard flow AutoCAD users already know — in a browser tab, nothing to install.
Metadata.ogAlt: A flange drawn in MellowCAD, with the words: Type L. Press Enter. Draw.
Metadata.appDescription: 2D drafting in the browser with AutoCAD commands, aliases and object snaps.

Commands.label: 01 · Muscle memory
Commands.title: The commands you know, down to the aliases.
Commands.lead: Type L for LINE, O for OFFSET, TR for TRIM. MellowCAD reads the same aliases, asks the same questions in the same order and takes the same option letters.
Commands.boardLabel: Commands and their aliases, grouped as on the ribbon
Commands.transcriptCaption: Replayed by the engine when this page was built. Same order, same option letters as AutoCAD.
Precision.label: 02 · Precision
Precision.title: Precision you can feel under the cursor.
Precision.lead: Object snaps, tracking and polar angles behave the way your hands expect. Each figure below is the editor's own frame, drawn by the engine mid-gesture.
Precision.osnapBody: {count, number} object snaps with AutoCAD's markers and tooltips. Shift+right-click forces one for the next pick — here, Tangent.
Precision.otrackBody: Rest on two points to acquire them, then follow their alignment paths to where they cross.
Precision.polarBody: Polar holds the rubber band to your increment and reads out distance and angle. Ortho locks it square.
Precision.selectionBody: Drag right for a window that takes what it encloses; drag left for a crossing that takes whatever it touches.
Precision.dynamicInput: Coordinates are typed the AutoCAD way: @100<30 for relative polar, #120,80 for absolute — right at the cursor.
Precision.osnapAlt: A line being drawn to a circle, snapped to the tangent point, with the Tangent marker and tooltip.
Precision.otrackAlt: Two acquired endpoints and their dotted alignment paths crossing at the cursor.
Precision.polarAlt: A line locked to the 30 degree polar ray, with its distance and angle tooltip.
Precision.windowAlt: A blue window lasso dragged from left to right round a circle, across a line, with the circle it takes highlighted.
Precision.crossingAlt: A green, dashed crossing lasso dragged from right to left round a circle, across a line, with both highlighted.
Toolset.label: 03 · Toolset
Toolset.title: A real 2D drafting toolset — and growing.
Toolset.lead: {commands, number} commands today, filed the way the ribbon files them. Each asks AutoCAD's questions in AutoCAD's order; the options still missing are tracked on the roadmap.
Toolset.drawBody: Lines, polylines with arc segments, circles, arcs and ellipses in all their constructions, splines, rectangles, polygons and hatches.
Toolset.modifyBody: Move, copy, rotate, scale, mirror, stretch; offset, trim, extend, fillet, chamfer, break and join; rectangular, polar and path arrays.
Toolset.annotateBody: Single-line and multiline text, and a full family of dimensions — linear, aligned, radius, diameter, angular, baseline and continue — with text and dimension styles.
Toolset.organizeBody: Layers, {linetypes, number} linetypes, {lineweights, number} lineweights and colours, with ByLayer throughout; blocks you can define, insert and purge, with attributes filled in at insertion.
Toolset.inquiryBody: Distance and area readouts, zoom and pan, undo and redo, snap mode and FROM.
Toolset.filesBody: Autosave, save and open a file, and the clipboard — copy, cut, paste and copy with base point.
Toolset.drawAlt: A slotted plate: a polyline with two arc ends and two holes.
Toolset.modifyAlt: Four concentric outlines, each offset from the last.
Toolset.annotateAlt: A stepped profile dimensioned with a linear dimension continued twice.
Toolset.organizeAlt: A rectangle with a hidden-line slot and a centre line, each on its own layer.
Toolset.inquiryAlt: A distance being measured corner to corner, with its distance, angle and deltas.
Toolset.filesAlt: A hatched circle and a pasted copy of it following the cursor.
LocalFirst.label: 04 · Local-first
LocalFirst.title: Your drawings stay on your device.
LocalFirst.autosaveBody: Every change is saved on this device as you draw. Close the tab; the drawing is there when you come back.
LocalFirst.fileTitle: A file when you want one
LocalFirst.fileBody: Ctrl+S saves the drawing as a file in MellowCAD's own versioned format. Ctrl+O opens it again, on any computer.
LocalFirst.privateBody: There is nothing to sign up for and your drawings are never sent anywhere. Analytics count page views without cookies.
LocalFirst.warning: Clearing this site's data clears the autosave too. Press Ctrl+S to keep a file.
LocalFirst.diagramAlt: Inside your device, the editor autosaves to the browser and saves to and opens a file; nothing leaves the device.
Engine.label: 05 · Engine
Engine.title: Not a drawing toy. A CAD engine.
Engine.lead: Underneath the canvas is an engine with no idea there is a browser around it — which is what lets it draw the figures on this page at build time.
Engine.kernelBody: Vectors, arcs, ellipses, intersections and offsets with no hidden state, tested by property as well as by example.
Engine.undoBody: Every change to the drawing is a command in the history, so Ctrl+Z always takes back exactly what you did.
Engine.formatBody: Versioned and tolerant: a file from an older release always opens, and a damaged object is skipped, not fatal.
Engine.fidelityBody: Command names, prompt order, keywords and defaults follow current AutoCAD. A partial command is fine; a reinvented one is not.
Engine.testsBody: Tools are tested the way you use them — moving, clicking and typing at a headless engine.
Engine.sourceBody: The code is on <github>GitHub</github> under the MIT licence, and the engine underneath is <npm>{package}</npm> on npm, to build your own tools on: <docs>its documentation</docs> shows how.
Engine.diagramAlt: The engine's five layers stacked, adapters on top and geometry at the bottom, with a dimension reading: imports point down.

Faq.label: 07 · FAQ
Faq.title: Questions, answered.
Faq.a1: Yes — free to use, with no account and no trial. It's an independent project under active development.
Faq.a2: Yes. The code is on <github>GitHub</github> under the MIT licence, and the engine is published on npm as <npm>{package}</npm>. The licence covers the code, not the MellowCAD name or logo.
Faq.q3: Do I need to install anything?
Faq.a3: No. It runs in a modern desktop browser — Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. Open mellowcad.com/draw and type a command.
Faq.q4: Does it really work like AutoCAD?
Faq.a4: That's the spec: commands, aliases, prompt order, option letters and defaults follow current AutoCAD. Some commands are still partial, and the roadmap lists exactly which options are missing.
Faq.q5: Can I open or save DWG or DXF files?
Faq.a5: Not yet. Drawings are saved in MellowCAD's own versioned file format. DXF import and export are on the roadmap but not scheduled yet.
Faq.a6: On your device. MellowCAD autosaves in your browser and never uploads your drawings. Clearing the site's data deletes the autosave, so press Ctrl+S to keep a file.
Faq.a7: No. It's an independent project. AutoCAD is a registered trademark of Autodesk, Inc.
Faq.q8: Does it work on tablets or phones?
Faq.a8: It opens, but it's built for a keyboard and mouse, like AutoCAD. Use a computer.
Faq.a9: {commands, number} commands, including LINE, PLINE, CIRCLE, ARC, ELLIPSE, HATCH, OFFSET, TRIM, FILLET, ARRAY, dimensions, blocks and layers. The full list, with aliases, is above.

Privacy.metaDescription: What MellowCAD keeps in your browser, what it measures, who handles that data and on what grounds, and your rights.
Privacy.label: Privacy
Privacy.title: What stays where.
Privacy.lead: MellowCAD has no accounts and no servers that see your drawings. This is everything it keeps, everything it measures, and who handles it.
Privacy.stored1: Your drawing, autosaved in the browser's local storage as you work. It never leaves the device.
Privacy.stored2: Nothing else, and no cookies. The live sketch on the home page keeps its drawing in the page's memory and forgets it when you leave.
Privacy.storedNote: Clearing this site's data in your browser deletes the autosave. Press Ctrl+S in the editor to keep a file.
Privacy.analytics1: Vercel Web Analytics counts page views: the page, the page you came from, your country and city, and your browser, system and type of device. It sets no cookies; a visit is recognised by a hash of the request, discarded after 24 hours, and the statistics are anonymous.
Privacy.analytics2: Vercel Speed Insights reports how fast pages load and respond, with the page, your browser, system, type of device, network speed and country — anonymously too.
Privacy.analytics3: Neither sees your drawings, and neither is used for advertising, profiling or any automated decision.
Privacy.handled1: MellowCAD is an independent project by {name}, who is responsible for this data and answers at <email>{address}</email>.
Privacy.handled2: Serving the site and measuring its use and speed rest on a legitimate interest in running a free service well, kept to anonymous statistics (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR).
Privacy.handled3: Vercel Inc. hosts the site and runs both measurements. Like any host, it processes your IP address to deliver the pages. It is based in the United States and certified under the EU–U.S. Data Privacy Framework.
Privacy.handled4: If you write, your message is handled by Google, the email provider, and used only to answer you, for as long as the conversation needs.
Privacy.rights1: You can ask to access, correct or delete data about you, to restrict or object to its use, or to receive a copy of it: write to the address above.
Privacy.rights2: You can also complain to a data protection authority — in the EU, the one where you live or work.

Docs.shortcuts.help: Opens the help of the running command in a new tab, or these docs with none.
Docs.shortcuts.enter: Runs what is typed. With nothing typed it takes the prompt's default or ends the command, and with no command running it repeats the last one.
Docs.shortcuts.escape: Cancels the running command; a first Esc clears what is half typed.
Docs.shortcuts.recall: With no command running, brings back the commands typed before.
Docs.shortcuts.complete: Completes the command name being typed; at a point prompt, steps through the object snaps under the cursor.
Docs.shortcuts.cycle: Steps through the overlapping objects under the cursor while selection cycling shows its badge.
